record.paper_title: Open Problems in Geometry and Topology
record.original_question: Let M be a closed, connected, oriented, irreducible 3-manifold. Must exactly one of the following alternatives hold: (a) M is isometric to a quotient S^3/Γ of the round 3-sphere by a subgroup Γ of Isom(S^3); (b) the fundamental group π1(M) contains a subgroup isomorphic to Z ⊕ Z; or (c) M is isometric to a quotient H^3/Γ of hyperbolic 3-space by a subgroup Γ of Isom(H^3)?

evidence.quote: Thurston's Geometrization Conjecture: Let M be a closed, connected, oriented, irreducible 3-manifold. Then precisely one of the following holds: a) M = S^3/Γ, where Γ ⊂ Isom(S^3). b) Z ⊕ Z ⊂ π1(M). c) M = H^3/Γ, where Γ ⊂ Isom(H^3).

artifact.status_search_result: This is Thurston's Geometrization Conjecture (in its dichotomy form for closed irreducible oriented 3-manifolds). It was proven by Grigori Perelman in 2002–2003 using Ricci flow with surgery, building on Hamilton's program. The proof has been verified in detailed expositions by Kleiner–Lott, Morgan–Tian, and Cao–Zhu.
